project.title: Bat, ball and bricks
project.about: A bat you slide left and right with the joystick, a ball, and a wall of bricks. Every brick the ball hits is rubbed out and scores a point; clear them all and a new wall appears. A starting point: change anything you like.
data: * A 16x16 drawing is four 8x8 blocks: top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right.
* A brick is one picture, two 8x8 pieces wide. Redraw it (or point the tile at another picture) to make something else.

catalogue.name: Change the score
catalogue.about: Adds a number to the score (use a negative number to take points away).

catalogue.name: Bounce off the walls
catalogue.about: If the thing reaches the left, right or top wall, it bounces back (it turns round and stays inside).

catalogue.name: If a thing goes past the bottom
catalogue.about: Checks whether a thing has gone lower than a line on the screen. If so, the blocks inside run.

catalogue.name: If all the tiles are gone
catalogue.about: Runs the blocks inside once the last tile of that kind has been hit. Put "Fill an area with tiles" inside to start a new wall.

catalogue.name: If two things touch
catalogue.about: Checks whether two things overlap. If they do, the blocks inside run.

catalogue.name: Keep moving at its speed
catalogue.about: Every frame, moves the thing by its speed (see "Set how fast a thing moves").

catalogue.name: Move with the joystick
catalogue.about: Left and right on joystick 1 slide the thing sideways. It stops at the two ends you choose.

catalogue.name: Put a thing here
catalogue.about: Puts a thing at a spot on the screen (x across, y down) and stops it moving.

catalogue.name: Play a sound
catalogue.about: Starts one of the sounds in your file (a block marked @sound).

catalogue.name: Set the screen colour
catalogue.about: Sets the colour of the screen behind everything else (pick any colour except see-through).

catalogue.name: Set how fast a thing moves
catalogue.about: Sets how many dots a thing moves each frame, across (negative = left) and down (negative = up).

catalogue.name: Show the score
catalogue.about: Writes the score as three digits on the screen (column across, row down).

catalogue.name: Fill an area with tiles
catalogue.about: Covers part of the screen with rows of a tile (any picture you draw, in 8x8 pieces: a brick, an alien, a crate). Tiles are drawn on the screen, not as sprites, so there can be as many as you like. Every row can have its own colour. The game keeps count of how many are left.

across.about: How many tiles in each row (0 = as many as fit)

top.about: How far down the screen it starts, in rows of 8 dots

left.about: How far across it starts, in columns of 8 dots

colour.zero: A different colour for each row
colour.about: One colour for every row, or a different colour for each row

stagger.about: Shift every other row by half a tile, like a brick wall
options: Every other row shifted by half a tile

catalogue.name: If a thing hits a tile
catalogue.about: Looks at the tile under the middle of the thing. If there is one, the whole tile is rubbed out, the thing can bounce (by default the way it came in: off the side if it came from the side, off the bottom if it came from below), and the blocks inside run (for the score and a sound).

options: Bounce off it, the way it came in
bounce.about: What the thing does when it hits a tile

catalogue.name: When one thing hits another
catalogue.about: Checks whether two things touch. If they do, the first one bounces off, is destroyed, or stops, and then the blocks inside run (for the score and a sound). When it bounces you choose which way it goes and at what angle.

thing.about: The thing that moves (for example the ball)

other.about: The thing it hits (for example the bat)

way.about: Which way it goes after the bounce
options: Straight back the way it came

angle.about: How steeply it goes after the bounce
options: Depends where it hit (the edges send it sideways)

asm:
* Bat, ball and bricks (made by Retro ASM Game Blocks; you can edit this file freely).
* Each [bracketed note] shows which block wrote the lines under it.

        DEF   START
        AORG  >A000             ; Fixed place in the extra memory, so "Run in MAME" can load it
VDPWD   EQU   >8C00             ; Video chip: write a byte of data
VDPWA   EQU   >8C02             ; Video chip: set the address (or a register)
VDPST   EQU   >8802             ; Video chip: read its status

START   LWPI  WS
        LIMI  0
        LI    R0,>01E2          ; Register 1: screen on, 16x16 sprites
        BL    @VWREG
        LI    R0,>0506          ; Register 5: the sprite list is at >0300
        BL    @VWREG
        LI    R0,>0602          ; Register 6: sprite drawings start at >1000 (the tile drawings use >0800 to >0FFF)
        BL    @VWREG
        LI    R0,>030E          ; Register 3: the colour table is at >0380
        BL    @VWREG
        CLR   R0                ; Clear the screen: 768 spaces from the top
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        LI    R0,>4000
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        LI    R1,>2000
        LI    R2,768
CLRSCR  MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        DEC   R2
        JNE   CLRSCR
        LI    R0,>4380          ; Colour table: white on see-through, so the screen colour shows
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        LI    R1,>F000
        LI    R2,32
CLRCOL  MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        DEC   R2
        JNE   CLRCOL
        LI    R0,>1000          ; Copy the drawing of bat to video memory
        LI    R1,BAT_PIC
        LI    R2,32
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>1020          ; Copy the drawing of ball to video memory
        LI    R1,BALL_PIC
        LI    R2,32
        BL    @VMBW
* [Set the screen colour]
        LI    R0,>0704          ; Register 7: the screen colour
        BL    @VWREG
* [Fill an area with tiles]
* Row 1 of tiles
        LI    R0,>0B00          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 96 to 97
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>038C          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>8000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,97
        LI    R1,>6000
        LI    R2,15
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 2 of tiles (shifted half a tile)
        LI    R0,>0B40          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 104 to 105
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>038D          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>A000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,129
        LI    R1,>6900
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,130
        LI    R1,>6800
        LI    R2,14
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,158
        LI    R1,>6800
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 3 of tiles
        LI    R0,>0B80          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 112 to 113
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>038E          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>B000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,161
        LI    R1,>7000
        LI    R2,15
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 4 of tiles (shifted half a tile)
        LI    R0,>0BC0          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 120 to 121
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>038F          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>2000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,193
        LI    R1,>7900
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,194
        LI    R1,>7800
        LI    R2,14
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,222
        LI    R1,>7800
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 5 of tiles
        LI    R0,>0C00          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 128 to 129
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>0390          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>7000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,225
        LI    R1,>8000
        LI    R2,15
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 6 of tiles (shifted half a tile)
        LI    R0,>0C40          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 136 to 137
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>0391          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>5000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,257
        LI    R1,>8900
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,258
        LI    R1,>8800
        LI    R2,14
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,286
        LI    R1,>8800
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R1,93             ; Tiles in the area
        MOV   R1,@BRICK_LEFT
* [Put a thing here]
        LI    R1,120
        MOV   R1,@BAT_X
        LI    R1,168
        MOV   R1,@BAT_Y
        CLR   @BAT_VX
        CLR   @BAT_VY
* [Put a thing here]
        LI    R1,124
        MOV   R1,@BALL_X
        LI    R1,80
        MOV   R1,@BALL_Y
        CLR   @BALL_VX
        CLR   @BALL_VY
* [Set how fast a thing moves]
        LI    R1,2
        MOV   R1,@BALL_VX
        LI    R1,2
        MOV   R1,@BALL_VY

* ---- once every frame (60 times a second) ----
MAIN    MOVB  @VDPST,R0         ; Wait for the next frame
        JLT   GO
        JMP   MAIN
GO
* [Quit: holding FCTN and = together goes back to the title screen]
        LI    R12,>0024         ; Look at keyboard column 0
        CLR   R1
        LDCR  R1,3
        LI    R12,>0006
        STCR  R1,8              ; Read the 8 switches (0 means pressed)
        ANDI  R1,>1100          ; FCTN and = both pressed?
        JNE   NOQUIT
        BLWP  @>0000            ; Start the console over: the title screen
NOQUIT
* [Move with the joystick]
        LI    R12,>0024         ; Look at the keyboard column that holds joystick 1
        LI    R1,>0600
        LDCR  R1,3
        LI    R12,>0006
        STCR  R1,8              ; Read the 8 switches (0 means pressed)
        INV   R1                ; Now 1 means pressed
        MOV   @BAT_X,R2
        COC   @KLEFT,R1         ; Pushed left?
        JNE   NOL1
        AI    R2,-4
NOL1    COC   @KRIGHT,R1        ; Pushed right?
        JNE   NOR2
        AI    R2,4
NOR2    CI    R2,8              ; Keep it between the two ends
        JGT   OKL3
        LI    R2,8
OKL3    CI    R2,232
        JLT   OKH4
        LI    R2,232
OKH4    MOV   R2,@BAT_X
* [Keep moving at its speed]
        A     @BALL_VX,@BALL_X
        A     @BALL_VY,@BALL_Y
* [Bounce off the walls]
        MOV   @BALL_X,R1
        CI    R1,8              ; Past the left wall?
        JGT   BW5
        LI    R1,8
        MOV   R1,@BALL_X
        NEG   @BALL_VX
BW5     MOV   @BALL_X,R1
        CI    R1,240            ; Past the right wall?
        JLT   BW6
        LI    R1,240
        MOV   R1,@BALL_X
        NEG   @BALL_VX
BW6     MOV   @BALL_Y,R1
        CI    R1,8              ; Past the top?
        JGT   BW7
        LI    R1,8
        MOV   R1,@BALL_Y
        NEG   @BALL_VY
BW7
* [When one thing hits another]
        MOV   @BAT_X,R2
        AI    R2,16
        C     R2,@BALL_X
        JH    HIT9              ; Overlapping so far?
        B     @NOHIT8
HIT9    MOV   @BALL_X,R2
        AI    R2,8
        C     R2,@BAT_X
        JH    HIT10
        B     @NOHIT8
HIT10
        MOV   @BAT_Y,R2
        AI    R2,4
        C     R2,@BALL_Y
        JH    HIT11             ; Overlapping so far?
        B     @NOHIT8
HIT11   MOV   @BALL_Y,R2
        AI    R2,8
        C     R2,@BAT_Y
        JH    HIT12
        B     @NOHIT8
HIT12
        ABS   @BALL_VY
        NEG   @BALL_VY          ; Going up
        MOV   @BALL_X,R1
        AI    R1,4              ; Middle of the thing
        MOV   @BAT_X,R2
        AI    R2,8              ; Middle of what it hit
        S     R2,R1             ; How far off the middle
        SRA   R1,2              ; A quarter of that is the sideways speed
        CI    R1,3
        JLT   WLO13
        JEQ   WLO13
        LI    R1,3              ; At most 3
WLO13   CI    R1,-3
        JGT   WHI14
        JEQ   WHI14
        LI    R1,-3             ; At least -3
WHI14   MOV   R1,@BALL_VX
        MOV   @BAT_Y,R1
        AI    R1,-8
        MOV   R1,@BALL_Y        ; Just above it
* [Change the score]
        INC   @SCORE
* [Play a sound]
        LI    R1,BOING
        MOV   R1,@SNDPTR
        CLR   @SNDWT
NOHIT8
* [If a thing hits a tile]
        MOV   @BALL_X,R5
        AI    R5,4              ; Middle of the thing
        SRL   R5,3              ; Column on the screen (8 dots each)
        MOV   @BALL_Y,R6
        AI    R6,5
        SRL   R6,3              ; Row on the screen
        MOV   R6,R0
        SLA   R0,5              ; Row x 32
        A     R5,R0             ; Screen position
        CI    R0,768
        JL    INSCR16           ; Still on the screen?
        B     @NOTILE15
INSCR16 MOV   R0,R4             ; Remember where
        BL    @VSBR             ; Which character is there?
        SRL   R1,8
        AI    R1,-96            ; This tile uses characters 96 to 143
        CI    R1,48
        JL    TILE17            ; A piece of this tile?
        B     @NOTILE15
TILE17  ANDI  R1,7              ; Which piece of the tile it is
        MOV   R1,R2
        ANDI  R2,1              ; Column of pieces
        SRL   R1,1              ; Row of pieces
        SLA   R1,5              ; Row x 32
        A     R1,R2
        S     R2,R4             ; Back to the top-left piece of the tile
        MOV   R4,R0             ; Rub out the whole tile (spaces)
        LI    R1,>2000
        LI    R2,2
        BL    @VFILL
        DEC   @BRICK_LEFT
        MOV   @BALL_X,R0        ; Where was the middle of it a moment ago?
        S     @BALL_VX,R0
        AI    R0,4
        SRL   R0,3              ; Column before
        MOV   @BALL_Y,R1
        S     @BALL_VY,R1
        AI    R1,5
        SRL   R1,3              ; Row before
        C     R0,R5             ; Same column as now?
        JEQ   SAMECOL18
        C     R1,R6             ; Different column. Same row?
        JEQ   SIDE19
        NEG   @BALL_VY          ; Came in at a corner: bounce back both ways
SIDE19  NEG   @BALL_VX          ; Came in from the side: bounce sideways
        JMP   BOUNCED20
SAMECOL18 NEG   @BALL_VY        ; Came in from above or below: bounce up or down
BOUNCED20
* [Change the score]
        INC   @SCORE
* [Play a sound]
        LI    R1,BOING
        MOV   R1,@SNDPTR
        CLR   @SNDWT
NOTILE15
* [If all the tiles are gone]
        MOV   @BRICK_LEFT,@BRICK_LEFT ; Any tiles left?
        JEQ   NOTILES22
        B     @TILES21
NOTILES22
* [Fill an area with tiles]
* Row 1 of tiles
        LI    R0,>0B00          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 96 to 97
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>038C          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>8000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,97
        LI    R1,>6000
        LI    R2,15
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 2 of tiles (shifted half a tile)
        LI    R0,>0B40          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 104 to 105
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>038D          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>A000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,129
        LI    R1,>6900
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,130
        LI    R1,>6800
        LI    R2,14
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,158
        LI    R1,>6800
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 3 of tiles
        LI    R0,>0B80          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 112 to 113
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>038E          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>B000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,161
        LI    R1,>7000
        LI    R2,15
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 4 of tiles (shifted half a tile)
        LI    R0,>0BC0          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 120 to 121
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>038F          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>2000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,193
        LI    R1,>7900
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,194
        LI    R1,>7800
        LI    R2,14
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,222
        LI    R1,>7800
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 5 of tiles
        LI    R0,>0C00          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 128 to 129
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>0390          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>7000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,225
        LI    R1,>8000
        LI    R2,15
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
* Row 6 of tiles (shifted half a tile)
        LI    R0,>0C40          ; Drawing of the tile for screen characters 136 to 137
        LI    R1,BRICK_PIC
        LI    R2,16
        BL    @VMBW
        LI    R0,>0391          ; Colour of those characters
        LI    R1,>5000
        BL    @VSBW
        LI    R0,257
        LI    R1,>8900
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,258
        LI    R1,>8800
        LI    R2,14
        LI    R3,2
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R0,286
        LI    R1,>8800
        LI    R2,1
        LI    R3,1
        BL    @VTILES
        LI    R1,93             ; Tiles in the area
        MOV   R1,@BRICK_LEFT
* [Put a thing here]
        LI    R1,124
        MOV   R1,@BALL_X
        LI    R1,80
        MOV   R1,@BALL_Y
        CLR   @BALL_VX
        CLR   @BALL_VY
* [Set how fast a thing moves]
        LI    R1,2
        MOV   R1,@BALL_VX
        LI    R1,2
        MOV   R1,@BALL_VY
TILES21
* [If a thing goes past the bottom]
        MOV   @BALL_Y,R1
        CI    R1,184            ; Lower than the line?
        JGT   LOW24
        B     @NOLOW23          ; No: skip the blocks inside (a far jump, so they can be as long as you like)
LOW24
* [Put a thing here]
        LI    R1,124
        MOV   R1,@BALL_X
        LI    R1,80
        MOV   R1,@BALL_Y
        CLR   @BALL_VX
        CLR   @BALL_VY
* [Set how fast a thing moves]
        LI    R1,2
        MOV   R1,@BALL_VX
        LI    R1,2
        MOV   R1,@BALL_VY
* [Change the score]
        LI    R1,-1
        A     R1,@SCORE
        JGT   SCOK25
        JEQ   SCOK25
        CLR   @SCORE            ; No negative scores
SCOK25
NOLOW23
* [Show the score]
        MOV   @SCORE,R0
        LI    R1,1              ; Screen position = row x 32 + column
        BL    @SHOWNUM
* [Show everything on the screen]
        CLR   R0                ; Sprite list starts at >0300
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        LI    R0,>4300
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        MOV   @BAT_Y,R1         ; bat
        SWPB  R1
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        MOV   @BAT_X,R1
        SWPB  R1
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        LI    R1,>0000          ; Which drawing
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        LI    R1,>0F00          ; Colour
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        MOV   @BALL_Y,R1        ; ball
        SWPB  R1
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        MOV   @BALL_X,R1
        SWPB  R1
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        LI    R1,>0400          ; Which drawing
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        LI    R1,>0A00          ; Colour
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        LI    R1,>D000          ; End of the sprite list
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        BL    @SNDTICK          ; Keep any sound going
        B     @MAIN

* ---- shared routines ----
* VWREG: set a video register. R0 holds the register number (left byte) and value (right byte).
VWREG   ORI   R0,>8000
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        B     *R11
* VMBW: copy R2 bytes from R1 to video memory address R0.
VMBW    ORI   R0,>4000
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
VMBW1   MOVB  *R1+,@VDPWD
        DEC   R2
        JNE   VMBW1
        B     *R11

* VTILES: draw R2 tiles side by side from screen position R0. Each tile is R3 pieces: the screen character in
* the left byte of R1, then the next one, and so on; the next tile starts again at R1.
VTILES  ORI   R0,>4000
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
VTL1    MOV   R1,R4             ; The first piece of this tile
        MOV   R3,R5
VTL2    MOVB  R4,@VDPWD
        AI    R4,>0100
        DEC   R5
        JNE   VTL2
        DEC   R2
        JNE   VTL1
        B     *R11

* VSBW: write the tile in the left byte of R1 to screen position R0.
VSBW    ORI   R0,>4000
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        ANDI  R0,>3FFF
        B     *R11

* The joystick switches: which bit means left, and which means right.
KLEFT   DATA  >0200
KRIGHT  DATA  >0400

* SNDTICK: called once a frame. Plays the next step of the current sound list, if one is playing.
SNDTICK MOV   @SNDWT,@SNDWT     ; Still waiting?
        JEQ   SND1
        DEC   @SNDWT
        B     *R11
SND1    MOV   @SNDPTR,R0        ; Where are we in the list? (0 = nothing playing)
        JEQ   SNDEND
        MOVB  *R0+,R2           ; How many bytes for the sound chip
        JEQ   SNDOFF            ; A count of 0 ends the list
        SRL   R2,8
SND2    MOVB  *R0+,@>8400       ; Send a byte to the sound chip
        DEC   R2
        JNE   SND2
        MOVB  *R0+,R2           ; How long to wait
        SRL   R2,8
        MOV   R2,@SNDWT
        MOV   R0,@SNDPTR
SNDEND  B     *R11
SNDOFF  CLR   @SNDPTR
        B     *R11

* VSBR: read the tile at screen position R0 into the left byte of R1.
VSBR    SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        NOP
        MOVB  @>8800,R1         ; Video chip: read a byte
        B     *R11

* VFILL: put the tile in the left byte of R1 in R2 screen positions in a row, starting at R0.
VFILL   ORI   R0,>4000
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
VFL1    MOVB  R1,@VDPWD
        DEC   R2
        JNE   VFL1
        B     *R11

* SHOWNUM: R0 = the number (0-999), R1 = screen position. Writes three digits.
SHOWNUM MOV   R11,R9
        MOV   R1,R4             ; Keep the screen position
        CLR   R2
        MOV   R0,R3             ; R2:R3 is the number to divide
        LI    R5,100
        DIV   R5,R2             ; R2 = hundreds, R3 = the rest
        MOV   R2,R6
        CLR   R2
        LI    R5,10
        DIV   R5,R2             ; R2 = tens, R3 = ones
        MOV   R2,R7
        MOV   R3,R8
        MOV   R4,R0
        ORI   R0,>4000
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        SWPB  R0
        MOVB  R0,@VDPWA
        AI    R6,>30            ; Digit characters start at 48
        SWPB  R6
        MOVB  R6,@VDPWD
        AI    R7,>30
        SWPB  R7
        MOVB  R7,@VDPWD
        AI    R8,>30
        SWPB  R8
        MOVB  R8,@VDPWD
        B     *R9

* A 16x16 drawing is four 8x8 blocks: top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right.
* @sprite 16x16
BAT_PIC BYTE >FF,>FF,>FF,>FF,>00,>00,>00,>00
       BYTE >00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00
       BYTE >FF,>FF,>FF,>FF,>00,>00,>00,>00
       BYTE >00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00

* @sprite 16x16
BALL_PIC BYTE >3C,>7E,>FF,>FF,>FF,>FF,>7E,>3C
       BYTE >00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00
       BYTE >00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00
       BYTE >00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00,>00

* @sound
BOING  BYTE 3,>8E,>0F,>90,4
       BYTE 3,>87,>0B,>90,4
       BYTE 1,>9F,1
       BYTE 0
       EVEN

* A brick is one picture, two 8x8 pieces wide. Redraw it (or point the tile at another picture) to make something else.
* @sprite 16x8 cells
BRICK_PIC BYTE >FF,>FF,>FF,>FF,>FF,>FF,>FF,>00
       BYTE >FE,>FE,>FE,>FE,>FE,>FE,>FE,>00

* @sprite 16x8 rows
ROWS_PIC BYTE 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
       BYTE 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
        END   START
